6. Complete campaign and cost accounting

Including restoration, independent references, load-source preparation, stock handling and analysis gives:

Proposed 500-case campaign ledger	Value
Equipment time	255.27 h
Elapsed allowance including offline preparation/analysis	291.27 h
Purchased process electricity	107.70 kWh
Human work	108.61 h
Initial campaign stock cash	$160,904
Stock consumed	$118,130
Unused ready spare value remaining	$42,774
Complete campaign cost, excluding first build	$146,849
First build, including independent load apparatus	$968,812

Consumed stock includes five jaws, ten pods, five foot receivers, five tool couplings, five rejected primary-kit bodies, sixteen bolt sets and the foot-cut consumables. The inventory calculation has no stockout and requires 30 quarantine positions.

That closes the accounting under its stated rules. It does not establish physical rack restoration or service life.

The estimated field deployment provides a 6 kW electrical connection allowance. The full campaign model averages approximately 0.42 kW over equipment time. Neither is a measured machine service map.

Repeat manufacture and lifetime

At production quantity 100, the repeat-installed estimate is $359,134. It includes manufacture, yield allowance, assembly, installation, controls, service interfaces, gantry, recovery dock, reference equipment, racks and contingency.

The financial model uses 20 years and 8% real discount. Components have separate finite replacement policies. For example, the twenty-four circulating jaws are assigned 2,500 uses each, equivalent to 5,000 global exchanges with two alternating sets. That life is an introduced economic policy, not demonstrated durability.

At 5,000 conditional episodes/year, the model gives $42.37/episode. Major annual costs include:

Annual item	Cost
Capital recovery	$36,579
Scheduled component replacements	$64,794
Rare failed jaw/pod/foot/tool packages	$63,500
Primary-kit and bolt-set renewals	$20,500
Rejected primary kits	$7,500
Labor, external calibration, floor, working stock, cleaning and other costs	Remaining balance

Electricity is a minor term. Replacement hardware and capital dominate.

The cost per physically accepted complete exchange remains unknown.
